title: Supported local perfect restriction and its stabilization
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $W$ an open and $T\subseteq X$ any subset. Choose derived localizations in Hom universe $w$ on $X,W$ and their localized open sites [def-pc-derived-category]. Let $R\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ have strictly perfect neighbourhood models [def-pc-perfect-complex] at every point of $W$, and suppose every cohomology stalk vanishes on $W\setminus T$. Put $F=J_W(R)$ for canonical derived open restriction [def-pc-derived-open-restriction-maps]. Both $F$ and $F\oplus F[1]$ are perfect on $W$, and all their cohomology stalks vanish at every $x\in W$ with $x\notin T$.

source.place: Definition-perfect and restriction of the models; stabilization as used in Tag 09IM

proof.text:
At x in W, intersect its given neighbourhood O with W. Apply the existing restrict_strictlyPerfect and restrict_model helpers from
PerfectCommonAffineModels to restrict K to this intersection and transport it through the equivalence between the
localized site and the open scheme. Restriction and this equivalence carry finite free
modules to finite free modules, preserve their retract equations, and preserve zero
terms. The exact restriction composition comparison therefore gives a strictly perfect
model for the restriction of R near x. Apply the existing perfect_shift helper from PerfectTwoOutOfThree with shift one;
its shifted local models have degree bounds a-1 and b-1 and reindexed finite free retracts. The split
biproduct triangle with first term F, middle term F plus F[1], and last term F[1]
is distinguished. Apply perfect two-out-of-three to obtain perfectness of the middle term.
Exactness identifies homology of the restriction with
restriction of homology. The stalk comparison identifies its stalk at x with the ambient
stalk at x.val, which is zero off T by hRT. Homology of a biproduct is the biproduct of
homologies, and homology of a shift is the shifted homology; both summands thus have zero
stalks off T. This proves both support clauses. The construction is pointwise and includes
empty W and empty support without any choice of a point.

mathlib_searches.query: Restriction to an open subscheme preserves locally perfect complexes and vanishing homology stalks; affine supported extension plus shift
A perfect complex restricts to a perfect complex on an open subscheme; the direct sum with its shift has the same closed support.
